report:
Conclusion: the claim is accurate for the U.S. FDA-approved indication. The FDA label states: “Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years” and to replace it after 5 years if continued contraception is desired (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf). The current prescribing information repeats this and describes the supporting evidence: a clinical trial enrolling generally healthy women aged 18–35, of whom 1,452 received Kyleena, with a 3-year core phase plus optional extension to 5 years (https://labeling.bayerhealthcare.com/html/products/pi/Kyleena_PI.pdf). Bayer’s HCP efficacy summary reports “>99% efficacy for each year of use” over 5 years in that population (https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy). The 2016 approval announcement likewise framed Kyleena 19.5 mg as reversible, long-acting pregnancy prevention for up to five years (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html).

Important boundaries: “approved up to five years” is not a guarantee for every user, nor evidence of effectiveness beyond year five. It requires correct insertion by a clinician, checking threads/position as advised, and timely removal/replacement; pregnancy can occur soon after removal. The label also carries contraindications and risks such as ectopic pregnancy, pelvic infection, perforation, expulsion, bleeding-pattern changes, and ovarian cysts. Overall, regulatory labeling and the cited phase 3 data strongly support the five-year prevention claim.
